item.title: Kano Assembly approves state police
item.description: By Hadiza Yusuf The Kano State House of Assembly has approved the proposed constitutional amendment to allow state governments to establish and operate their own police forces. The approval was confirmed by the Majority Leader of the Assembly, Lawan Hussaini Dala, shortly after plenary on Tuesday. Dala said the lawmakers had considered and approved the proposed constitutional review to provide for the establishment of state police. “We have approved the constitutional review for the establishment of state police at plenary today,” he said. The approval followed deliberations on the proposed amendments to the 1999 Constitution, as amended, which seek to give state governments the legal authority to establish and operate their own police forces. During plenary, the lawmakers considered the constitutional alteration bill in the Committee of the Whole, deliberating on clauses one to 26 of the proposed amendment. The lawmakers had earlier adopted a motion to consider the constitutional amendment bill in the Committee of the Whole before proceeding with deliberations on its provisions. item.title: Tinubu needs another term to consolidate reforms — Tompolo
item.description: …Presents 30 vehicles for mobilisation By Obas Esiedesa, Abuja Ahead of the 2027 presidential election, High Chief Government Ekpemupolo, popularly known as Tompolo, has mobilised support for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election in Imo State, declaring that the President means well for Nigeria and deserves another four years to consolidate his administration’s reforms. Tompolo made the declaration on Tuesday at the inauguration of the PBAT Door-to-Door Movement in Imo State, where he donated 30 vehicles to facilitate grassroots mobilisation for Tinubu’s re-election. Represented by the Managing Director of Tantita Security Services Limited, Chief Kestin Pondi, Tompolo said the vehicles and other resources were provided to support Governor Hope Uzodimma and the movement’s campaign activities across the state. He described Tinubu as a courageous leader who prioritised Nigeria’s interests by embarking on economic reforms from the beginning of his administration in May 2023. “Our President, President Bola Tinubu, is a very courageous man. A man who puts Nigeria first. A man who loves Nigeria more than he loves himself. “A man who loves Nigeria more than the office that he is vying for. When he came into office, he did not do the normal calculations that politicians usually do. He came in and said that he wants to reform Nigeria,” Tompolo said. Relaying Tompolo’s message, Pondi said the donation was aimed at strengthening the movement’s capacity to mobilise voters for the President across the state. “Your Excellency, we have come with vehicles. We have come with resources. These vehicles you have seen, there are 30 of them. We brought them to Imo State to support you in your cause to re-elect President Bola Tinubu,” he said. Tompolo said the movement would work with Uzodimma and other political leaders to take the President’s campaign to households and communities across Imo State, adding that the newly inaugurated chapter would be available to support campaign activities whenever required. “Your Excellency, the PBAT Door-to-Door Movement in Imo State is at your beck and call. Anytime you need them, call them. Give them instructions. Tell them how you want them to campaign,” he said. Speaking at the event, Governor Uzodimma commended Tompolo for providing resources to support the campaign, describing the movement as an important partner in efforts to secure another term for Tinubu. Uzodimma said his assessment of the President’s performance had convinced him that Tinubu should be given another term to complete his programmes and initiatives. “When we preach the Gospel about the All Progressives Congress government of President Bola Tinubu, we started, we were not many. But as the days go by, the efforts and activities of the government begin to trickle in. Nigerians begin to see the man called Bola Tinubu in his true colour,” he said. item.title: US Visa Bond: Full list of countries, including Nigeria, required to pay up to $20,000
item.description: The United States has listed 50 countries whose citizens must pay a visa bond of up to $20,000 when applying for certain visitor visas, including Nigeria, according to the US Department of State. The measure applies to eligible applicants for B-1 business and B-2 tourist visas travelling on passports issued by the listed countries. The bond amounts are $10,000, $15,000 or $20,000, with the specific amount determined by a consular officer during the visa interview. In a notice published on October 2, 2026, the Department of State outlined the countries subject to the visa bond programme and their respective implementation dates. The programme operates under Section 221(g)(3) of the Immigration and Nationality Act, with the department stating that the requirement applies regardless of where an applicant submits their visa application. item.title: Senate Passes bill to jail oil polluters, impose heavier fine
item.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA- THE Senate has passed a bill that would strengthen the National Oil Spill Detection and Response Agency (NOSDRA) with powers to impose heavier fines and criminal penalties for oil spill violations. The bill is titled National Oil Spill Detection and Response Agency (Establishment) Act (Amendment) Bill, 2026, was passed after the Senate adopted the report of its Committee on Environment. The bill seeks to amend the NOSDRA Establishment Act 2006 to provide statutory backing for adequate fines and criminal sanctions to enforce environmental laws in the petroleum sector. In his presentation of the report, Chairman Senator Olubiyi Fadeyi, Senate Chief Whip Senator Tahir Monguno (Borno North) said the amendment addresses persistent pollution in the Niger Delta. He said oil spills have continued to devastate the environment and destroy livelihoods, particularly fishing and farming, in oil-producing communities. According to Monguno, existing penalties have failed to deter offenders, necessitating tougher sanctions. “The fines are not deterrent enough to deter offenders,” he told the Senate, adding that the bill introduces criminal liability for spills that damage the environment and deprive residents of their means of livelihood. The Senate dissolved into Committee of the Whole to consider the bill clause by clause and approved Clauses 1 to 12, including the short title, explanatory memorandum and long title. Upon reverting to plenary, the Senate read the bill a third time and passed it. The law is expected to boost NOSDRA’s enforcement capacity and provide a stronger framework for tackling oil spill violations. The President Godswill Akpabio hailed the Environment Committee for its work and congratulated NOSDRA on the additional powers granted by the legislation. item.title: Jigawa Assembly approves constitutional amendment for state police
item.description: ‎By Muhammad Inuwa, Dutse The Jigawa State House of Assembly has approved the proposed constitutional amendment seeking the establishment of state police in Nigeria. The Speaker of the House, Haruna Aliyu Dangyatin, announced the approval during plenary, saying the move was aimed at strengthening community policing and improving security across the country. He explained that the proposed amendment was transmitted to the state Assembly for consideration after its passage by the Senate and the House of Representatives. ‎According to him, the establishment of state police would help address security challenges at the grassroots by giving state governments greater responsibility for protecting lives and property. The approval is part of ongoing efforts to decentralise Nigeria’s policing system and strengthen the capacity of states to respond to security threats within their jurisdictions. The development comes after the National Assembly gave state Houses of Assembly a 30-day deadline to communicate their positions on the proposed constitutional amendment. State legislatures were directed to indicate whether they supported or opposed the bill as part of the constitutional amendment process. item.title: ‘Toluwanisings should be buried in his home, not cemetery’ – Grandma
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye The paternal grandmother of late gospel singer Olayemi Bayonile Bolaji, popularly known as Toluwanisings, has alleged that he rarely supported her financially before his death while opposing plans to bury him in a cemetery. The elderly woman, identified as Sabitiyu Olayemi, made the claims in a trending social media interview with journalist Dunmininu in Osun. The interview was conducted in Yoruba. She said Toluwanisings was born in Kano and also narrated how she helped care for the singer and his mother before he moved to Lagos, but had not seen him for more than five years. “Sodiq was born in Kano, that was where his naming cermony was conducted. We have been taking care of Sodiq (Toluwanisings) and his mother even before he went to Lagos. He attended Arabic schools. When he was in grammar school, I would visit him” she said, in Yoruba language. The grandmother also revealed that she knew he was a musician but did not know he had built a house or held a housewarming ceremony. She recalled that he once visited her with his wife and first child, but alleged that they had been out of touch for years. “I just knew he is a musician. I am not aware he built a house; I was not aware of a housewarming. Even if I want to call him, they will say I shouldn’t. It’s been a long time I saw him. It has been over five years I set my eyes on him,” the grandmother said. She said she eventually asked someone in the village to help her call him. “So I called and told him it was me. He responded, ‘Ahh, Mummy.’ I told him that you cannot even check up on me. He said it is work that has been a hindrance,” she recounted. According to her, Toluwanisings sent her ₦10,000 on about three occasions after that conversation, but did not send money again. She also alleged that when her phone was damaged and she sought help contacting him about a replacement, his elder sibling told her not to call him. Asked whether he sent her medication or money for medical expenses, she replied: “There is nothing Sodiq (Toluwanisings) sends to me.” Despite her allegations, she said his death deeply affected her as she broke down in tears during the interview. “When I heard that he had died, I felt so sad. Whether I benefited from him or not, he is still my child. I have accepted my fate. I wish God had taken me so I would not have had to witness this tragedy,” she said, breaking down in tears. The grandmother also objected to burying the singer in a cemetery, saying he should be laid to rest at his home. “I do not agree that Toluwanisings should be buried in a cemetery. They should bury him at his house. They should not come and bury him close to his mother,” she said. Toluwanisings’ family announced that the singer died in the early hours of October 14, 2026 at the age of 41, but did not disclose the cause of death. item.title: 2027: APM in coalition talks, says Daura
item.description: By Juliet Umeh Vice-presidential candidate of the Allied Peoples Movement, APM, Lawal Daura, says the party is involved in coalition discussions ahead of the 2027 general elections. Daura disclosed this on Channels Television’s Sunrise Daily, where he also called for an inclusive approach to governance, saying Nigeria needed a “reset” to address what he described as recurring political and social problems. “We are involved right now in the discussion for the coalition,” he said. Explaining the APM’s “reset agenda,” Daura said Nigeria had been “moving in cycles without really making much or any progress.” He said the agenda would bring Nigerians together to discuss the country’s direction and agree on how it should be governed. “The reset agenda should be an all-inclusive thing. Let us get together as Nigerians.” According to him, a government formed under the agenda would involve stakeholders beyond those who helped it win an election. “Where you make an election or win your election to be the winner-takes-all is not going to help Nigeria,” he said. Daura, a former Director-General of the Department of State Services, said his decision to enter politics was motivated by his desire to contribute to the country’s development. “I felt maybe there is a need for me to come out and contribute,” he said, adding that joining the political process would allow him to contribute “more and better than when it is just maybe by the sidelines.” He said his years in public service had given him insights into the country’s challenges, but added: “I play politics, but within the definition given by politicians in Nigeria, I would say I am not a politician.” Daura said he initially sought the governorship of Katsina State after senior citizens approached him over insecurity in the state, which he described as an “epicentre” of banditry and kidnapping. “I have made myself very clear right from the onset that whatever my people requested me to do, I would do. At my level, I can even become a local government chairman. I wouldn’t mind.” He said his governorship bid through the African Democratic Congress did not proceed as he had hoped, citing the absence of primaries and concerns about compliance with electoral law. He said he declined suggestions that he seek a Senate seat instead. Daura said he chose the APM after considering other parties, which he alleged faced internal leadership disputes or court cases. He called the APM “the only healthy party” at the time he joined and said it was expanding its reach. “Right now, as I speak, APM is a party to beat,” he said. item.title: Fubara Reaffirms Support For Tinubu, Wike-Led Rainbow Coalition
item.description: Rivers State Governor, Siminalayi Fubara, has reaffirmed his support for President Bola Tinubu and the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, pledging to work for the victory of the Rainbow Coalition in the 2027 general elections. Fubara spoke on Tuesday at the unveiling of the coalition’s candidates in Rivers State, where he urged members to put past leadership disputes behind them and work together. The governor described the coalition as family, expressing happiness at being reunited with political allies after a crisis that divided the group. “I’m really happy to be here, not just being here, but standing in the midst of my family,” he said. Fubara acknowledged Wike and other political leaders for their roles in his emergence as governor, expressing gratitude that they had come together again for what he described as the collective good of Rivers State. He pledged to support the coalition’s candidates, saying he would do everything within his power to secure their victory. The governor also thanked Tinubu for standing by him during his most difficult period and reaffirmed his commitment to the political bloc led by Wike. “I’m here with all my heart, my soul, and my body, and I will do everything within my power to ensure that we have victory, not just for Mr President, who has stood for me in my most difficult time, but also to ensure that this power still remains in our own bloc,” Fubara said. He described the unveiling as an honour and expressed optimism about the candidates’ performance in the January 2027 elections. The Rainbow Coalition comprises seven political parties that have aligned to field consensus candidates for the elections in Rivers State. They are the All Progressives Congress (APC), Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), Action Alliance (AA), All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA), Labour Party (LP), Allied Peoples Movement (APM) and Boot Party. However, candidates from only the APC and PDP emerged as the coalition’s consensus candidates for the 2027 elections. The coalition, led by Wike, who is also the national leader of the PDP, unveiled its candidates at a ceremony in Port Harcourt on Tuesday. Former Minority Leader of the House of Representatives, Kingsley Chinda, emerged as the coalition’s governorship candidate on the APC platform, with the current Majority Leader of the Rivers State House of Assembly, Major Jack, as his running mate. For the three senatorial districts, the APC has two candidates, while the PDP has one. Felix Amaechi Obua is the APC candidate for Rivers West, while Senator Allwell Onyesoh is the party’s candidate for Rivers East. Senator Olaka Nwogu of the PDP is the candidate for Rivers South-East. The coalition’s House of Representatives list has 13 candidates, comprising 10 APC members and three PDP members. item.title: ADC-PCC to N’Assembly: Reject Tinubu’s $21bn loan over lack of transparency
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike The African Democratic Congress Presidential Campaign Council (ADC-PCC) has urged the National Assembly to reject President Bola Tinubu’s proposed $20 billion and £1 billion foreign borrowing unless the Federal Government provides full details of the facilities and demonstrates their benefits to Nigerians. The council said the fresh borrowing would add to the burden on Nigerians already battling rising living costs and increased taxation, questioning why the government was seeking more loans without accounting for previous borrowings and savings from fuel subsidy removal. In a statement by its Director of Media and Publicity, Kola Ologbondiyan, the ADC-PCC faulted the administration’s borrowing plans, demanding evidence that the funds would translate into tangible improvements in citizens’ lives. “What exactly is President Tinubu borrowing all this money for? Where are the roads, the electricity, the hospitals, the jobs and the critical infrastructure that should justify this relentless accumulation of debt? Nigerians deserve answers,” Ologbondiyan said. He questioned why the government was returning to international creditors while millions of Nigerians struggled to survive the effects of its economic policies. The council warned that continued borrowing without transparent spending and measurable returns could deepen Nigeria’s debt burden, restrict future governments’ policy options and threaten the country’s economic sovereignty. “This is not a sustainable path to national development. It is a dangerous attempt to mortgage the future of Nigeria and generations yet unborn,” Ologbondiyan said. The ADC-PCC demanded that Tinubu publish a comprehensive account of all domestic and foreign borrowing since May 29, 2023, including a breakdown of revenue realised from subsidy removal and how the funds had been spent. It also called for full disclosure of the proposed loans’ purposes, interest rates, repayment periods, fees, conditions and any collateral or guarantees attached to the facilities. “Nigeria cannot borrow its way out of poor economic management. Borrowing must be tied to clearly defined national priorities, transparent expenditure and measurable outcomes. Anything less is an injustice to the Nigerian people,” the council said. It urged lawmakers to insist on accountability and refuse to approve the facilities until the Federal Government establishes their necessity, sustainability and tangible benefits to Nigerians. item.title: Nasarawa NDC Publicity Secretary quits party, declares support for SDP candidate
item.description: By Edwin Philip, Lafia The Publicity Secretary of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in Nasarawa State, Mr Joseph Danjuma, has resigned from the party and declared support for the Social Democratic Party (SDP) governorship candidate, former Inspector-General of Police, Abubakar Adamu. Danjuma announced his resignation in a letter titled “Letter of Resignation” addressed to the state chairman of the NDC, citing a lack of opportunity to perform his duties as the party’s spokesperson. “I wish to humbly resign my membership and position as the Publicity Secretary of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Nasarawa State Chapter, with immediate effect,” he stated. Explaining his decision, he added: “My decision follows the lack of opportunity to perform my role as the spokesperson of the party in the state.” Following his resignation, Danjuma declared his intention to join Adamu’s campaign ahead of the 2027 governorship election. “With this development, I hereby fully join the campaign train of Ex-IGP Adamu. Thank you,” he said. Danjuma, a journalist who has worked with print and broadcast media organisations, previously served as Chief Press Secretary to former Nasarawa State Deputy Governor, Hon. Dameshi Luka. He had earlier expressed support for Adamu at a rally organised under the auspices of the Alago Support Group. Speaking at the event, Danjuma said the group was formed out of a desire for the Alago people to participate actively in decisions concerning the political future of Nasarawa State. He said the group considered Adamu a suitable candidate based on his record of public service and experience as a former police chief. Danjuma also highlighted Adamu’s connections with the Alago community, noting that he had attended school with some prominent sons and daughters of the area in Obi and had maternal ties to the people. “We have resolved that we will no longer be onlookers or fence-sitters while the political destiny of our dear state is being decided. The time to participate, to take a stand and to take our destiny in our own hands is now,” he said. He maintained that members of the Alago community should be free to support candidates of their choice, citing Section 40 of the 1999 Constitution, which guarantees freedom of peaceful assembly and association. Efforts to obtain a reaction from the NDC chairman in Nasarawa State, Hon. Dogo Shammah, regarding Danjuma’s resignation and his stated reason for leaving the party were unsuccessful as of the time of filing this report. item.title: Ebonyi Assembly passes State Police Bill
item.description: By Jeff Agbodo, Abakaliki The Ebonyi State House of Assembly has passed into law the State Police Bill transmitted to it by the National Assembly for concurrence. The bill seeks to alter the 1999 Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria (as amended) to provide a legal framework for the establishment of State Police Services across the federation, while retaining the Nigeria Police Force at the federal level. The State Assembly, during plenary at the Assembly Complex, Nkaliki Road, Abakaliki, saw all 24 members vote unanimously in favour of the bill after extensive deliberations and consultations with their constituents. The Speaker of the House, Rt. Hon. Moses Ije Odunwa, who presided over the session, said the unanimous vote underscored the Assembly’s commitment to constitutional reforms aimed at strengthening security architecture, enhancing access to criminal intelligence and protection of lives and property. Odunwa noted that the demand for a sub-national policing system has been a long-standing clamour among Ebonyi people, adding that the state had formally presented its position in support of State Police during the public hearing organised by the National Assembly on the constitution review. “The passage of this bill reflects the wishes of Ebonyians who desire a policing system that is closer to the people and more responsive to local security challenges,” the Speaker stated. The Leader of the House and member representing Afikpo North-West Constituency Hon. Kingsley Ikoro, in his contribution said the establishment of State Police would significantly increase manpower and improve effectiveness in tackling crime and criminality at the grassroots. Also speaking, Hon. Victor Chidi Nwoke, representing Abakaliki North Constituency, Hon. Oluchukwu Ukie Ezeali, representing Afikpo North East Constituency, and the Chief Whip of the House, Hon. Nkemka Okoro Onumah, in their separate contributions, emphasised the need to bring policing closer to the people as a panacea to the nation’s security challenges. Following the passage, the Speaker directed the Clerk of the House, Mrs. Uche Edene, to transmit a formal memo communicating the resolution of the House to the National Assembly. item.title: 2027: Atiku Not A Man You Can Take His Word To The Bank – Wike
item.description: The Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, has questioned the credibility of former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar, accusing him of frequently changing his position on political matters. Wike spoke on Tuesday at the unveiling of candidates of the Rivers State Rainbow Coalition, where he criticised the consistency of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate. Drawing on his past political dealings with Atiku, Wike recalled supporting the former vice-president’s presidential ambition in 2019 and running against him in the Peoples Democratic Party’s (PDP) presidential primary in 2022. “I pray you never know him, [Atiku Abubakar]. I ran with him in the 2022 presidential primaries. In 2019, I was one of the biggest sponsors for that presidential election,” he said. Wike questioned Atiku’s reliability, declaring, “He’s not a man that you can go to the bank with his words.” ﻿ The minister alleged that Atiku frequently changed his position, making it difficult to rely on his statements. “He tells you one thing in the morning, he tells you another thing in the afternoon. He tells you something in the evening, the next morning he tells you a different thing,” Wike said. item.title: Makinde camp asks EFCC to probe alleged payments for ministerial appointments
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike The Makinde-Daura Presidential Campaign Organisation has called on the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) to investigate allegations that serving ministers paid billions of naira to secure appointments in President Bola Tinubu’s administration. The organisation, which is campaigning for Seyi Makinde under the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), said the President’s silence five days after Tinubu campaign spokesperson Alwan Hassan reportedly made the revelation on national television had raised concerns about possible high-level complicity. In a statement by its Director of Strategic Communications, Richard Nnanna Ihediwa, the campaign organisation accused the President of failing to address an allegation it said raised fundamental questions about the integrity of ministerial appointments and the conduct of his administration. “Mr. President’s silence validates public apprehension that either he is not in control or he sits in approval of a corrupt and fraudulent system where public offices are reduced to commodities sold to highest bidders,” the statement said. The organisation further alleged that a cabal of APC leaders in the National Assembly, senior presidential aides and individuals close to Tinubu had usurped government responsibilities, paving the way for the appointment of people it described as incompetent and corrupt. It blamed the administration for worsening insecurity and economic hardship, warning that alleged diversion of public resources could further undermine efforts to address Nigeria’s infrastructure deficit. “The EFCC must identify all those involved in this bribe for appointment scandal and ensure that anyone found culpable is held accountable in accordance with the law,” the organisation said. It urged Nigerians not to lose faith in the country ahead of the 2027 presidential election, promising that a Makinde-Daura government would prioritise transparency, accountability, service delivery and citizens’ welfare under its proposed four-year ‘Reset Nigeria’ agenda. item.title: Atiku to Tinubu: $20.5bn loan plan vindicates my warning
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike Former Vice President and African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, has said President Bola Tinubu’s request for approval to borrow $20.52 billion and €1.045 billion vindicates his earlier warning about a proposed $20 billion loan, accusing the administration of failing to disclose the specific projects the funds would finance. Atiku said the absence of project-by-project details raises questions about transparency and the possibility of public funds being channelled to political allies and favoured contractors, particularly through the Lagos–Calabar Coastal Highway project, which he alleged had been rerouted inland. In a statement by Phrank Shaibu, Director of Strategic Communication of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, Atiku recalled that he had warned on October 12 about the reported borrowing plan and challenged Tinubu to confirm or deny it and publish the relevant accounts. “Today, he has asked the Senate to approve $20.52 billion and €1.045 billion in external loans. My warning has been vindicated,” he said. Atiku faulted the President for failing to provide details of the projects, their costs, locations and contractors, insisting that Nigerians should not be asked to shoulder such a huge debt without knowing how the money would be spent. He questioned whether the highway project could become a conduit for directing borrowed funds to political allies, especially with an election approaching. “Is this a development plan for Nigerians or a campaign financing scheme dressed up as infrastructure?” he asked. The ADC candidate warned that he would scrutinise loans obtained during the final year of Tinubu’s administration if elected President, vowing to challenge any borrowing found to have breached constitutional, statutory or due process requirements. “I put local and international lenders on notice: any loan granted to this winding-down administration must meet all constitutional, statutory and due process requirements,” he said. He urged the National Assembly to withhold approval until the President publishes the projects, contracts, costs, contractors, loan terms and repayment obligations attached to the borrowing plan. “No public money should be borrowed in the dark, and no lawmaker should sign a blank cheque against Nigeria’s future,” Atiku said. He said the burden of proof rested on Tinubu to demonstrate that the loans would serve the national interest rather than political interests, warning that Nigerians struggling with the cost of living should not be made to pay for debts incurred without adequate public disclosure. Atiku said the controversy could further shape the political contest, with voters having an opportunity to hold the administration accountable for its borrowing decisions. item.title: US arrests Nigerian man who fled to Nigeria in 2019 over money laundering
item.description: A 34-year-old Nigerian man, Adetunji Abudu, has been arrested in the United States over an alleged money laundering conspiracy involving millions of dollars obtained through fraud schemes targeting elderly Americans. Abudu, from Lagos, Nigeria, was arrested on Monday night at Logan Airport in Boston, Massachusetts, while attempting to re-enter the United States from Istanbul, Turkey. According to a statement from US authorities, he appeared before the US District Court in Rhode Island on October 21, 2026, and was ordered detained pending trial. He is one of six defendants charged in a superseding indictment returned by a federal grand jury in Providence over an alleged conspiracy to launder proceeds from multiple fraud schemes operated from Nigeria. The schemes allegedly targeted elderly US residents through online romance scams, fraudulent sweepstakes, false rental listings and sham online shipping transactions. According to the indictment, money obtained from victims was allegedly channelled through bank accounts and businesses in Rhode Island, Idaho and other locations, with significant proceeds ultimately transferred to Nigeria. Members of the alleged conspiracy were also accused of purchasing vehicles with illicit proceeds and shipping them overseas. US authorities said Abudu fled the country to Nigeria in 2019 after the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) executed a court-authorised search of his residence in North Providence. Five of his co-defendants — Dotun Olawale Alonge, Oluwaseyi Akintol, Samson Ikotun, Olabode Shaba and Oladipup Shodipu — have since pleaded guilty to money laundering conspiracy. They received sentences ranging from time served to 42 months’ imprisonment, according to the statement. The case is being prosecuted by Assistant US Attorney John P. McAdams. The FBI investigated the matter with assistance from the US Postal Inspection Service and the Tallmadge Police Department in Ohio and the Moscow Police Department in Idaho. The allegations against Abudu remain unproven in court. He is presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty. item.title: ADC explains Atiku’s crude subsidy plan
item.description: By Juliet Umeh The African Democratic Congress, ADC, Presidential Campaign Council says its candidate, Atiku Abubakar, would allocate a portion of Nigeria’s crude oil to domestic refineries at a reduced price, as part of a proposed production subsidy. One of the council’s spokespersons, Dr Uche Diala, said the proposal would reduce refineries’ input costs. He said it was different from subsidising imported fuel or giving crude to refiners free of charge. “We are saying that, to the extent that Nigerians need to consume and live, we will sell our share to participating domestic refineries at a reduced cost,” Diala said on Channels Television’s Sunrise Daily. “They will not buy it at the international price, and they will not buy it for free. It is a production subsidy at the production end, not a consumption or import subsidy.” Asked how the plan could be sustained, Diala said the government would first need to determine how much crude was available for domestic use after accounting for joint-venture commitments and other obligations. “We need to know what quantity of crude we have, and then it is from there that we start with the joint ventures,” he said, adding that the Petroleum Industry Act provided for domestic crude supply. Diala said the proposal would also require reviewing existing arrangements, including forward-sale agreements, and increasing production. He cited a 2026 budget benchmark of 1.8 million barrels per day, saying Nigeria could raise output to help sustain the plan. “We are doing about 1.6 million barrels a day. If we are serious-minded, we can scale up our production, and that would help to sustain the production subsidy,” he said. Diala also rejected allegations that ADC staff had gone unpaid for months, describing the claim by the All Progressives Congress as fabricated. “Our party workers are fine. They are getting their remuneration,” he said. He added that the party could provide payroll records if journalists requested them, but said the APC had no moral basis to demand the information. On the 2027 election, Diala said Atiku would accept defeat if he lost “fair and square,” but expressed confidence that the ADC candidate would win. “He is a democrat. I can assure you that Atiku Abubakar is going to win the election by the grace of God and the support of Nigerians.” The post ADC explains Atiku’s crude subsidy plan appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Northern youths demands Justice over killing of Sheikh Masusuka
item.description: By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo The Northern Youth Council of Nigeria (NYCN) has called on the Federal Government and the Katsina State Government to ensure a thorough investigation into the killing of Islamic scholar, Sheikh Yahaya Ibrahim Masusuka, and bring those responsible to justice. The council, in a statement issued on Monday by its president, Comrade Isah Abubakar, condemned the killing of the cleric, describing it as a grave attack on Islamic scholarship and the moral fabric of Northern Nigeria. According to reports, Sheikh Masusuka was shot dead at about 7:30 p.m. on Monday in front of his residence in Dutsin-Ma Local Government Area of Katsina State by gunmen riding on a motorcycle. His friend, identified as Adamu Abubakar, was also killed in the attack. Both men were reportedly taken to a hospital but were pronounced dead on arrival. The Katsina State Police Command said an investigation had commenced, while efforts were being made to apprehend the assailants. The identities of the attackers and the motive for the killings had yet to be established in the reports available. Reacting to the incident, the NYCN described the late cleric as a revered scholar and mentor whose teachings of the Holy Qur’an had inspired many people, particularly youths in the North. The council said the killing went beyond the loss of an individual, arguing that it represented an attack on religious scholarship, truth and the values that sustain society. It also expressed concern over what it described as the persistent problem of impunity surrounding high-profile killings in the country, urging the authorities to demonstrate their commitment to protecting citizens and ensuring accountability. The council called for a transparent and comprehensive investigation into the circumstances surrounding the assassination, including any possible security lapses and the existence of a wider conspiracy, if established by evidence. It further urged the authorities to look beyond the immediate perpetrators and investigate any individuals who may have financed, planned or facilitated the crime. According to the statement, justice would not be served by arresting only those who directly carried out the attack if further investigations established the involvement of other persons. “The era of empty promises, superficial condolence messages and decorative investigative committees is over,” the council said, insisting that the authorities must demonstrate the political will to ensure that those responsible are brought to justice. The NYCN said it would continue to monitor the investigation and called on the governments at both federal and state levels to ensure that the case was not abandoned. The council also prayed for the repose of the soul of the deceased cleric and asked Almighty Allah to comfort his family, associates and followers. It urged the security agencies to act swiftly and professionally to establish the circumstances surrounding the killing and prevent similar attacks

item.title: Tinubu not dodging responsibility over poverty, says Morka
item.description: By Juliet Umeh The All Progressives Congress (APC) spokesperson, Felix Morka, has said President Bola Tinubu is not avoiding responsibility for Nigeria’s poverty and hunger, arguing that the problems predate the current administration. Morka spoke on ARISE Television’s The Morning Show while responding to criticism of Tinubu’s remarks at the APC campaign flag-off in Kaduna State. The President had said he was working to address poverty and hunger inherited from previous administrations. Opposition figures had faulted the comment, saying Tinubu should focus on tackling hardship under his government rather than blaming past leaders. Morka said the President was placing the country’s economic challenges in historical context. “He was simply profiling the history of the endemic poverty that we are confronted with in our country. “Poverty has been with us for a very long time. The President was saying that the problem he is working hard to fix was created by some of those who today see poverty and hunger as though they descended on our country only in the last few years.” He said previous administrations had also failed to eradicate poverty, adding that the problem could not be resolved instantly. “All the other presidents who have come before them did not eradicate poverty. They couldn’t eradicate poverty. “There is no present without a past. The present is only the present because there is a past which this President was referring to,” he said. Asked about Tinubu’s 2023 campaign pledge to “conquer hunger,” and promises to support food security through agricultural hubs, storage facilities, processing plants and commodity exchanges, Morka argued that campaign goals were subject to gradual implementation. “When a president or anybody who is campaigning for office gives objectives, they are liable to progressive realisation. They are not an event,” he said, adding that Tinubu had not promised to eradicate poverty within his first months or years in office. The programme’s hosts challenged Morka to say when Nigerians could expect the President’s campaign pledges to be fulfilled, including a promise to create one million jobs in the digital economy. “The timeline is for the President to finish the job he has started,” Morka said, arguing that Tinubu was seeking another four-year term to complete his programme. During the exchange, a host cited figures indicating that poverty had risen from 56.2 percent in 2023 to 63 percent, and argued that the administration’s policies, including the removal of fuel subsidy and currency devaluation, had worsened hardship. Morka rejected the criticism, saying the administration had taken difficult decisions to address structural problems. He said subsidy removal had improved government revenue and that “a lot of the macroeconomic systems are now looking good.” The hosts also questioned the administration’s budget performance and asked what Nigerians had seen from the additional revenue.
